name: Battle of Marignano
note: The accounts give no compass directions for the field, so the plan is drawn with the Swiss coming from the left and the French facing them. The French guns are said to have stood in a crescent along the south-eastern and eastern edges of the vanguard; they are drawn here in front of the Landsknecht square, where the Swiss charged them. The accounts do not say where Bourbon's cavalry stood beyond the French right, nor where the Swiss second and third divisions stood, nor what troops the Venetians brought; Alencon's division is placed on the French left because the accounts call it the left-wing division when the Swiss attacked it. The fighting ran over two days and a night, and the Swiss withdrawal in a single square is drawn as three blocks falling back together.

phases.title: The French form up and the Swiss approach
phases.text: The French, who had not expected battle, formed in three divisions. The vanguard held two shallow rises with crossbowmen, a Landsknecht square and arquebusiers, the king's force stood two kilometres behind, and the Swiss came on in three divisions.
phases.quote: The French army quickly sprang into action, forming up in three divisions.

phases.title: The Swiss forlorn hope charges the guns
phases.text: A forlorn hope detached from the Swiss vanguard and charged the grand battery with lowered pikes. It drove back the Landsknecht defenders and captured a few of the guns, the speed of its advance making the French fire ineffective.
phases.quote: At first the Swiss attack succeeded in driving back the landsknecht defenders and capturing a few of the guns

phases.title: Bourbon's cavalry strikes the flank
phases.text: Cavalry from the French right counter-attacked the forlorn hope's flank and drove it back to the shelter of the Swiss vanguard.
phases.quote: cavalry from the French right counter-attacked their flank, driving the forlorn hope back to the shelter of the Swiss vanguard

phases.title: The pursuing French horse fall back
phases.text: The French horse that chased the forlorn hope were themselves forced to retreat a full kilometre after taking heavy losses.
phases.quote: The pursuing French horse were themselves forced to retreat back a full kilometer after taking heavy losses.

phases.title: Night fighting by moonlight
phases.text: Smoke and darkness hid the fighting. French cavalry charges, often led by the king himself with Bayard at his side, threw back temporary Swiss gains time and again, and the outcome hung in the balance.
phases.quote: Furious French cavalry charges, often led by the king himself, with Bayard at his side, succeeded time and again in throwing back temporary Swiss gains.

phases.title: The fighting stops in the darkest hours
phases.text: In the darkest hours the fighting stopped and both armies drew apart and reorganised. During the night some Swiss soldiers, and even whole units, slipped away from the field.
phases.quote: In the darkest hours, the fighting stopped, and both armies extracted themselves and reorganized.

phases.title: The Swiss charge the guns again at dawn
phases.text: The Swiss reformed their largest phalanx and charged the reassembled battery once more. Massed cannon fire slowed it, and though the Landsknechts were again driven back, the guns at point blank range stopped it pushing farther.
phases.quote: Again, the defending German landsknechts were driven back; but the massed fire of the guns at point blank range prevented the Swiss from pushing farther forward.

phases.title: Bayard's cavalry charge forces the Swiss back
phases.text: Another French cavalry charge, this time led by Bayard, forced the attacking Swiss to give ground after the guns had checked their advance at point blank range.
phases.quote: Still another French cavalry charge, this time led by Bayard, forced the attacking Swiss to give ground.

phases.title: The Swiss turn on the French left
phases.text: Baffled by the artillery, the Swiss turned their assault on Alençon's left-wing division. They made some headway, and the attack was then thrown back.
phases.quote: After making some headway, this attack too was thrown back.

phases.title: The Venetians arrive
phases.text: Allied Venetian forces under d'Alviano arrived in the mid-morning and turned the tide against the Swiss, whose attacks had been repulsed everywhere.
phases.quote: Only the mid-morning arrival of allied Venetian forces commanded by the condottiero Bartolomeo d'Alviano turned the tide against the Swiss.

phases.title: The Swiss withdraw in a single square
phases.text: With their ranks in bloody shambles, the Swiss gave ground grudgingly and withdrew by forming a single large open square, keeping strict discipline in their retreat.
phases.quote: they grudgingly gave ground and withdrew by forming a single gigantic open square, maintaining extraordinary discipline in their retreat
